title: Pharmacological conditioning as a drug dose reduction strategy in patients with psoriasis
summary: Learning mechanisms, such as the association between a stimulus (e.g. the appearance of a drug) and an effect (e.g. an improvement in symptoms), play an important role in medicine. In this study, we want to investigate whether these learning mechanisms can be used to reduce the dose of medication in the treatment of people suffering from psoriasis. This would have the advantage that a lower dose of expensive medication could be used, making treatment more accessible. We will randomly divide 168 patients into three groups. The first group will receive the same treatment as in normal clinical practice: one injection of 300mg secukinumab (an effective so-called biologic) at each of 8 time points. The people in groups 2 and 3 receive a reduced dose of medication in order to investigate how the effect can be increased using learning mechanisms. They receive the full dose only at the beginning of the study. Thereafter, group 2 alternates between 150mg of medication and placebo and group 3 receives 75mg of medication throughout. In this way, both groups receive the same amount of medication in total, but we can investigate the role of the administration scheme. People in both groups will also receive a special taste stimulus with each dose of medication to support the learning experience. The study will last a total of 20 weeks.

interventions.name: Pharmacological control: group 1; (TAU-treatment as usual) 300mg secukinumab (as in clinical routine, with weekly s.c. injections over 5 weeks (weeks 0-4), followed by three monthly injections (weeks 8, 12 and 16).

Partial reinforcement: group 2; acquisition phase lasting 2 weeks with two injections of 300mg secukinumab (weeks 0-1), followed by an experimental phase with alternating injections of placebo and 150mg secukinumab (weeks 2-4, 8, 12 and 16).

Continuous reinforcement: group 3; acquisition phase lasting 2 weeks with two injections of 300mg secukinumab (weeks 0-1), followed by an experimental phase with injections of 75mg secukinumab (weeks 2-4, 8, 12 and 16).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patient has had a diagnosis of chronic plaque psoriasis with a Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) >10 
- Patient is a candidate for systemic therapy 
- Women of childbearing potential: no pregnancy; negative serum pregnancy test before entering the study, agreement to use a highly effective method of contraception
Exclusion criteria:
- Forms of psoriasis other than chronic plaque psoriasis
- Pregnancy or breast feeding
- Insufficient ability to communicate in or understand German, dementia or (functional) analphabetism
- Lacking capacity to consent to study participation
- Existing contraindication to therapy with secukinumab according to the summary of product characteristics (like history of hypersensitivity to secukinumab or its excipients, chronic infections, like untreated (latent) tuberculosis, administration of live vaccines <6 weeks before therapy onset)
- Any medical or psychiatric condition which, in the Investigator’s opinion, would preclude the participant from adhering to the protocol or completing the study per protocol
- History of, respectively active, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
- Ongoing use of systemic anti-psoriatic treatments (concomitant topical treatment is allowed)
- Previous exposure to secukinumab
